design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 of meter_testing_and_metering (Kellerman Brothers Bakery LLC, referee backbill settlement).

[0] Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 4]}. Root meter_ext_referee_backbill_settlement takes 5 factors; prerequisite meter_ext_slow_meter_backbill takes 4. Multiset [4, 5] = draw.

[1] Why this is a good test. The caller asks one thing — settle the Commission referee result on the bakery's removed meter and accept it herself. Getting the settlement right forces the agent to (a) read the settlement rule's prerequisite sentence and see on the meter's adjustment record that the company's own slow result of 2026-08-14 was never backbilled, (b) work out from the slow-meter backbill rule that its write is the one that brings that state about, compute and record it, and (c) reprice the bills at the referee registration and subtract what now stands. Both computations reconcile a year of GD bills from another difficulty's ledger (energy, PSCR, demand, billing demand at the 25.0 kW minimum), read the meter's test history (no within-tolerance result, a utility-initiated request), date the error from the installation, apply the new-meter limit, correct only to the tolerance edge and, for the settlement, extend through the removal. Difficulty comes from reading policy and records and calculating, never from missing information or tool choice: each write has exactly one tool.

[2] Scope and headroom (principle C). Difficulty claims meter_test_request, meter_test_fee, meter_accuracy_adjustment, meter_installation_order, meter_order_cancellation, meter_opt_out_setup_fee, meter_opt_out_monthly_fee. Task 0 (first task) claims the two slow-side referee policies (company slow-meter backbill; customer-accepted referee backbill settlement) and their tools post_slow_meter_backbill_dc57beb1 (agent) and accept_referee_backbill_settlement_27524241 (user). Reserved for task 1 (draw: 3 prerequisite problems, factor counts [6, 6, 4, 5]): the fast side of a referee dispute (company fast-meter refund + customer-accepted referee refund settlement), the repeat test fee (whose return through a refund gives task 1 its second value_input edge) and the non-registering backbill on another meter of the same customer. Nothing of task 1's space is touched here.
Base defects routed around (recorded here because blueprint/ is frozen): (i) every amount-bearing meter event (meter_accuracy_adjustment, meter_test_fee, opt-out fees) declares a trigger into service (service_billing_credit / service_backbill_charge / service_program_debit). The service-side posting is governed by service_program_postings ("Amounts decided in another program are posted to the service agreement named on the originating record") and belongs to the service difficulty's tools; this difficulty's tools write only the originating meter row and never a service table. (ii) The meter category has no numeric field on a test request or an installation order, so the customer's own write in every task is the acceptance of a referee settlement (a meter_accuracy_adjustment row) rather than an order. (iii) customers.income_qualified_until is not readable by the computation DSL, so the opt-out fee policies (whose base fees turn on it) are not claimed by any task. (iv) The base adjustment period is a day-level midpoint; the computation DSL counts bills by whole months from the handling date, so the extended rules restate the period in whole billing months (declared in overwrite).

[3] Policies, base lineage, overrides. Both policies: subject [meter_accuracy_adjustment], base_policy_refs [meter_accuracy_adjustment_rule]. Inherited gate: adjust_each_result_once ("Each test result is adjusted once.") — the company result and the referee result are distinct results and each is adjusted once. Overwrite (declared clause by clause): the base period sentence (meter_msr_error_start_date, refund/backbill caps) is replaced by the whole-billing-month period; the base corrected-charges sentence (energy, demand, PSCR) by the standard energy+PSCR baseline with the demand ladder; the base amount sentence (registration to 100, adjusted_kwh) by the target-registration ladder and the rounded amount (the tools record no kWh); for the settlement also the posting sentence ("The refund is credited, and the backbill billed, on the service agreement on the adjustment date.") because the settlement is recorded only on the customer's acceptance. Not overridden: slow -> backbill direction, the type tolerance classes (meter_test_result_rule), the adjustment threshold, rates of each affected bill (billed amounts are used). Triggers: slow-meter backbill = state_due (a slow company result with no backbill is owed whether or not anyone calls); settlement = on_request (only when the customer accepts).

[4] Factor card (handling-time world).
 Slow-meter backbill (expected 41.98; all-baseline 92.94):
  - slow_backbill_months_reached [method, multi-source]: tiers {set by failed-meter replacement or test exchange AND no within-tolerance result -> months since installation; within-tolerance result AND schedule effective after it -> months since schedule; otherwise half}. World: installation_reason failed_meter_replacement, results only 2026-08-14 slow and 2026-09-03 slow -> 8 months. Baseline -> 4, result 30.18. Near-miss: the agreement's previous meter LPL-IDM-4471902 had a within-tolerance periodic result on 2023-03-14 — a reader who takes the agreement's latest within-tolerance test (instead of this meter's) falls to the fall-through.
  - slow_backbill_limit [parameter]: {installed < 12 months before test -> 6; >= 12 AND periodic test overdue -> 3; otherwise backbill_max_months 12}. World: 8 months -> 6. Baseline 12 -> result 56.81.
  - slow_backbill_demand_basis [method, cross-difficulty service]: {demand schedule AND bills at the minimum -> demand of bills above the minimum; demand schedule AND none at minimum -> all demand; otherwise none}. World: GD (11.84 USD/kW), bills 2026-02-20 and 2026-04-20 billed at 25.0 kW -> 2088.57 - 592.00 = 1496.57. Baseline none -> result 36.21. Near-miss: bills ending 2025-02-20 and 2025-04-20 were also billed at the minimum but fall outside the six-bill period.
  - slow_backbill_target_registration [parameter]: {utility-initiated request -> 100 - tolerance; periodic and no utility-initiated -> 100 - tolerance/2; otherwise 100}. World: request of 2026-08-07 is utility_initiated -> 99.0. Baseline 100 -> result 152.45. Near-miss: the commission_referee request (2026-08-19) is not a company-initiated test.
 Referee backbill settlement (expected 50.65; all-baseline 72.2): months (8, baseline 29.17), limit (6, baseline 77.68), demand basis (1914.52, baseline 37.22), target (99.0, baseline 184.91) as above, plus settlement_last_bill [method]: {removed after the company test -> add bills through the removal; still in service -> add every bill since; otherwise none}. World: removed 2026-08-26 > 2026-08-14 -> the bill ending 2026-08-20 is added; baseline -> result 34.49.
 Cross-difficulty reads (service): rate_effective_date, minimum_billing_demand_kw, demand_charge_usd_kw, service_bills energy/rider/demand/billing_demand_kw. No tier reads a stamp; the tiers rest on bills, test rows and installation dates.

[5] Base-invariant card. meter_accuracy_adjustment_rule.adjust_each_result_once (dedup, system_record, key meter_adjustments.meter_test_id): at frozen_time the adjustment record holds one row only (a619b1ec-05fa-4d25-a982-cfc55c7b2996, the Bridge St 2017 refund on meter_test_id e114938f-e7ea-4bce-ae18-4266cbe2c830); neither d2d82878-65e1-40c8-82a0-11b857bb172e nor ecae7247-e770-4f06-bac6-49369d6e1ee7 is adjusted, so both writes satisfy the gate; after step 9 the company result is adjusted and step 11 adjusts a different result. No time gate governs meter_accuracy_adjustment (temporal_feasibility = []). The referee request itself satisfied meter_test_request_rule at the time it was made (in_service meter, 5 days after the company test, inside the 30-day window) — recorded in seed_consistency, not re-decided.

[6] Business-object card. Target object: meter installation 1c90a6bd-21dd-46b7-aa3c-47b296be2f61 (LPL-IDM-5208836, AMI Interval Demand Meter) at agreement a3b3baab-5d5f-4cc4-aefb-20854675e672 (Schedule GD, 1140 Leonard St NW). Company result d2d82878-65e1-40c8-82a0-11b857bb172e (field, 2026-08-14, 98.62, slow) answers utility-initiated request 1dd2ec9d-3397-42d7-b9db-df545f626622; referee result ecae7247-e770-4f06-bac6-49369d6e1ee7 (shop, 2026-09-03, 98.31, slow) answers commission_referee request 9c9164f4-bfc2-4aa6-b413-b74e44eeb308. Bills included: regular bills of a3b3baab-5d5f-4cc4-aefb-20854675e672 ending 2026-02-20..2026-07-20 (backbill) and 2026-02-20..2026-08-20 (settlement). Excluded: bills ending before 2026-02-20 (beyond the six-bill limit), every bill of the closed Bridge St agreement, and the Bridge St 2017 refund (another meter, another agreement). Correlation key written back: meter_test_id of the result adjusted.

[7] Problem-tree card. Root P_R = meter_ext_referee_backbill_settlement (user tool). Edge P_R -> P_A (meter_ext_slow_meter_backbill), kind value_input, gate rs_already_backbilled, form state, prerequisite sentence (affirmative direction, the way a billing desk states what a figure rests on): "The referee backbill settlement is fixed only after the company test result it reviews carries its slow-meter backbill on the meter's adjustment record.". Four-point test: ordering connective "only after"; XX is a record-visible state (a backbill carried on the meter's adjustment record against the company result), no action named; no tool, id or code token; strength "only after", scope one company result. Exactly one write of this difficulty records a backbill against a company slow result: the slow-meter backbill tool (the settlement writes against the referee result, the other task-1 tools write refunds, fees or non-registering backbills). Derivation: sentence + find_meter_adjustments (no row for d2d82878-65e1-40c8-82a0-11b857bb172e) + the slow-meter backbill rule ("it is calculated for the company's own test result ... recorded on the meter's adjustment record against that test result, as a backbill") -> record the slow-meter backbill first. False at the opening: no meter_adjustments row carries d2d82878-65e1-40c8-82a0-11b857bb172e. Resolution order [P_A, P_R]. Deletion sensitivity: skipping step 9 makes the settlement 92.63 instead of 50.65. user_scenario mentions no prerequisite; tools validate none.

[8] Seed. Customer f3f5a5a4-34f8-4c6f-8e91-0450fe8233cf (business, since 2012-06-04, phone 6164402317, EIN last4 6148, ZIP 49504). Agreements: a3b3baab-5d5f-4cc4-aefb-20854675e672 GD active since 2019-04-01 (balance 0.00, autopay pays each bill on its due date); closed Bridge St GS agreement (2012-06-11..2019-04-05). Meters: Bridge St LPL-3PC-1180472 (2012-2017, fast 102.41 in 2017, refunded 291.87 — settled) and LPL-3PC-2093315 (2017-2019, within tolerance 2019); Leonard St LPL-IDM-4471902 (2019-03-28..2025-12-03, periodic within tolerance 2023-03-14, removed 2025-12-03 when its successor was set under a failed-meter replacement order; no accuracy result was recorded for it, so nothing on it is adjusted), LPL-IDM-5208836 (2025-12-03..2026-08-26, the disputed meter), LPL-IDM-5611407 (in service since 2026-08-26). 24 GD bills 2024-09-20..2026-08-20 computed with the GD tariff (energy 0.09104 summer / 0.08547 winter, demand 11.84 USD/kW on max(measured, 60% ratchet, 25 kW), PSCR 0.00387, customer 68.00), 24 autopay payments and the 2017 Bridge St meter-error refund credit. Rows that bear weight: the failed_meter_replacement reason and empty within-tolerance history (months, limit), the utility-initiated request (target), the two minimum-demand bills inside the period (demand), the removal date after the company test (last bill), the slow results (registrations) and the empty adjustment record (prerequisite). Automatic clauses checked: no unpaid bill (no late charge or notice owed), the slow meter was replaced within 8 business days (meter_exchange_on_failure_business_days 10), no opt-out or tampering clause fires.

[9] Persona design. Greta Kellerman, co-owner/bookkeeper, practical and tired; volunteers only: the August test said slow, she asked for a Commission referee test, the old meter came off August 26, the referee (early September) also said slow, she wants to settle and accept it herself today. Given on request: phone 6164402317 then EIN 6148 (ZIP and email if pressed), the meter is the one removed August 26. Passive: agrees if told something must be recorded first; runs the acceptance with exactly the figures given; closes on confirmation. No incidental asks.

[10] Standard solution. find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, 6148) -> find_service_accounts -> find_meter_installations -> find_meter_tests(customer) -> find_meter_adjustments(customer): nothing for the company result -> find_service_bills(GD agreement) -> find_service_credits(customer) -> compute and record the slow-meter backbill 41.98 -> compute the settlement on the world that now carries it: 50.65 -> hand the acceptance to the customer, who runs it.

[11] Verification. The computations were recomputed with check_compute's own evaluator (build_env/eval_compute) on the handling-time worlds: step 9 on initial_state, step 11 on initial_state + the step-9 row. Output: backbill 41.98 (factor baselines 30.18/56.81/36.21/152.45, all-baseline 92.94); settlement 50.65 (baselines 29.17/77.68/37.22/184.91/34.49, all-baseline 72.2); settlement without step 9 = 92.63.

[12] Easy mistakes. Taking the agreement's latest within-tolerance test (2023, previous meter) as the anchor; capping at 12 instead of the new-meter limit; leaving demand out or correcting the two minimum-demand bills' demand; correcting to 100 instead of 99.0; stopping the settlement at the company test date although the meter stayed in until 2026-08-26; settling before the company backbill stands (92.63, double recovery). Each is excluded by the rule text and the records alone.

[13] Draft recomputation from the visible context (hidden compute masked): from the settlement rule text, find_meter_tests and find_meter_adjustments the agent learns the company result needs its backbill first; from the backbill rule and the bills it obtains 8 -> 6 bills, 1496.57 demand, target 99.0 -> 41.98; then 7 bills, 98.31 -> 92.63 - 41.98 = 50.65. Agrees with gold.


[R2] Revision log (policy-task audit round 1, audits/policy_task/meter_testing_and_metering/0.md): task 0 had no RED item. Observation closed: the seed paragraph no longer asserts that the previous meter failed a test (no failing result is seeded); it states only the failed-meter replacement order of its successor. Charter changes of round 2 (repeat-fee count basis, refund months ladder) touch no task-0 policy; the slow-meter backbill and referee backbill settlement were re-emitted unchanged in content (YAML authoring comments dropped) and recompute to the same 41.98 / 50.65.
user_scenario:
You are Greta Kellerman, co-owner and bookkeeper of Kellerman Brothers Bakery LLC, the business on the Lakeshore Power & Light account, calling from the bakery office in the slow mid-morning stretch after the bread run. You are practical and a little worn out by this meter business; you keep your own ledger, you speak plainly and you do not like being bounced around.

What you know, and say near the start in your own words: back in August a Lakeshore crew tested the electric meter at the bakery on Leonard Street and said it was running slow. You did not believe it, so you asked the Public Service Commission for a referee test. The old meter came off on August 26 and the Commission's referee test was done in early September, and the letter you got afterwards says the referee test found the meter slow as well. You have decided not to fight it any further. You want to settle the referee result today: find out what the bakery owes for that old meter and accept it so the matter is closed. You do not know any dollar figure and you have no paperwork showing one.

You give the bakery's phone number first, 616-440-2317 (you say it with the dashes, but it is 6164402317). If the representative asks for another detail to confirm who you are, you give the last four of the bakery's EIN, 6148. Only if asked further, the billing ZIP is 49504 and the account email is books@kellermanbrothersbakery.com. The account is in the business name, Kellerman Brothers Bakery LLC, and the service address is 1140 Leonard St NW, Grand Rapids, MI 49504. If asked which meter, you only know it was the one taken out on August 26; you do not know meter numbers or reference numbers and you let the representative look them up. If asked what the referee found, you remember the letter said slow but you do not remember any percentage.

You are happy for the representative to record whatever Lakeshore has to record on the bakery's meter records to get the settlement worked out; if they tell you something else has to be put on the account first, you say that is fine and to go ahead. The acceptance itself you want to give yourself: once the representative tells you the settlement amount and hands the acceptance over to you, you accept the referee settlement exactly as they give it, with the meter, the referee result reference and the amount they read out, and you do not change any of it. If the amount surprises you, you say only that you have nothing to compare it with and you will take their word for it.

When the representative confirms the settlement is accepted and recorded, you thank them and end the call. You do not ask for a payment plan, a letter, a refund of anything or a change to the new meter, and you do not raise any other account question.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge, no parallel prerequisites: the slow-meter backbill must land before the settlement (the settlement subtracts every backbill standing on the meter). Writing the settlement first would compute it at 92.63 (nothing to subtract) and the later backbill 41.98 would double-recover; the prerequisite sentence fixes the order.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the step-9 slow-meter backbill leaves no backbill row on the meter and the settlement recomputes at 92.63 instead of 50.65 (rs_already_backbilled 0.00 instead of 41.98); the terminal adjustment record also lacks the 41.98 backbill row.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario speaks only of settling the referee result and accepting it; it never mentions the company's own test result being adjusted, a first backbill, an amount already recorded or anything that must be done first. The only related line is a passive reaction ('if they tell you something else has to be put on the account first, you say that is fine'), triggered by the agent's own statement.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: task_tools.py: accept_referee_backbill_settlement_27524241 creates its meter_adjustments row from its three arguments without reading any existing adjustment, and post_slow_meter_backbill_dc57beb1 likewise writes unconditionally; neither returns an error or hint when the other has or has not run.
